Alex, 

I'm happy to try, but once I got all of the extra packages installed I hit all kinds of parsing errors. NA Date values caused problems. Now non-NA datetime values are not parsing right. I seem to have fixed those, but there's no DEPTH in your sample dataset. 

library(lubridate)
library(sp)
library(tidyverse)

data2 <- read_csv("~/Downloads/Sample_7G_data.csv") %>%
filter(!is.na(LAT), !is.na(DATE))

coordinates(data2) <- c("LON","LAT")
proj4string(data2) <- CRS("+proj=longlat +datum=NAD83")  ## for example...not sure which projection this was in?

data2utm <- spTransform(data2, CRS("+proj=utm +zone=10 +ellps=GRS80 +towgs84=0,0,0,0,0,0,0 +units=m +no_defs"))

data2 <- as.tibble(data2utm) %>%
rename(Easting = LAT, Northing = LON) %>% #makes Lat and Lon = northing and easting
mutate(TIME = seconds_to_period(TIME) # make seconds into HMS
, TIME = sprintf('%02d:%02d:%02d', hour(TIME), minute(TIME), second(TIME)) # print it out as HH:MM:SS
, DATETIME = paste(DATE, TIME, sep=" ") # paste date and time together
, DATETIME = ymd_hms(DATETIME, tz="Etc/GMT-7"))  %>% # parse date into right time zone
distinct(TRANSMITTER, DATE, TIME, .keep_all = TRUE) # keep only unique TRANSxDATExTIME

parts:
Alex, 

This is what I'm thinking, but there's a few caveats to this approach. I've allocated your transmitters as shape. Once you get past six transmitters, you really won't be able to differentiate them easily. You could facet them by transmitter or facet them in groups of transmitters, if that makes sense for your data. The color I've repurposed to represent time, but scaling color by date is a PITA so I had to hack the breaks. This was the color changes as time goes on. Your example data doesn't show this (at all). 

You probably also want to show depth as well. We've used color and shape, so perhaps you could so size for depth, but that could lead to difficulty in interpretation. 

B

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(sp)
library(ggmap)

data2 <- read_csv("~/Downloads/Sample_7G_data (1).csv") %>%
filter(!is.na(LAT), !is.na(DATE)) %>%
mutate(LON2 = LON, LAT2 = LAT)

coordinates(data2) <- c("LON","LAT")
proj4string(data2) <- CRS("+proj=longlat +datum=NAD83")  ## for example...not sure which projection this was in?

data2utm <- spTransform(data2, CRS("+proj=utm +zone=10 +ellps=GRS80 +towgs84=0,0,0,0,0,0,0 +units=m +no_defs"))

data3 <- as.tibble(data2utm) %>%
dplyr::rename(Easting = LAT, Northing = LON) %>% #makes Lat and Lon = northing and easting
dplyr::mutate(TIME = seconds_to_period(TIME) # make seconds into HMS

, TIME = sprintf('%02d:%02d:%02d', hour(TIME), minute(TIME), second(TIME)) # print it out as HH:MM:SS
, DATETIME = paste(DATE, TIME, sep=" ") # paste date and time together
, parsed = ymd_hms(DATETIME, tz="Etc/GMT-7")
)  %>% # parse date into right time zone

dplyr::mutate(DEPTH = if_else(DEPTH > 0, DEPTH*-1, NA_real_)) %>% #Change depth to negative values, anything negative already will be NA, 0 will stay same
dplyr::distinct(TRANSMITTER, DATE, TIME, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% # keep only unique TRANSxDATExTIME
dplyr::arrange(parsed)

tags <- as.data.frame(table(data3$TRANSMITTER)); tags     # provides a list showing number of detections by transmitter


###########Plotting Trajectories on map #######################
# Get the basemap
#look at data to get coordinates
map <- get_map(location = c(lon = -122.47, lat = 37.81), zoom = 13, crop = T, scale = "auto", 
              color = "color", maptype = "satellite")  # can change to terrain
gg <- ggmap(map, extent = "panel", padding = 0)  # call the basemap

# Add points. Note plot will produce warnings for all points not in the
# lat/lon range of the base map layer.

#fortify data for plotting (make sure data is in POSIXct form, no NAs, and fortify data)

fortify(data3)

myBreaks <- function(x){
    breaks <- c(min(x),median(x),max(x))
    attr(breaks,"labels") <- as.POSIXct(breaks, tz = "Etc/GMT-7", origin = strptime("1970-01-01 00:00:00", "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"))
    names(breaks) <- attr(breaks,"labels")
    return(breaks)
}

###Plot
gg + geom_point(data = data3, aes(x=LON2, y = LAT2, shape = TRANSMITTER, colour = as.numeric(parsed))) +
    scale_colour_gradient(low="lightblue", high="red", breaks=myBreaks) +
    labs(color="Date")
